Do Now: Input and Data Types (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must what the user types be changed into a number before the program can do maths with it?Show the answer

What the user types arrives as text. The program must turn it into a number first.

4 minutes. From 2.1 and 2.2. Follow the program one line at a time.

item = input("Item? ")
price = float(input("Price? "))
print(item + " costs " + str(price * 2))

The user types: pen then 1.5

Total: 3 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: input and data types

steps.text: This is a different program. The user types Pai, then 30. Do the same steps with your program.
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = int(input("Temp? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 4))

steps.text: Line 1: the first thing typed goes into city. city holds "Pai".
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = int(input("Temp? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 4))
city: "Pai", text

steps.text: Line 2: int() turns "30" into a whole number. temp holds 30, a whole number.
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = int(input("Temp? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 4))
temp: 30, a whole number

steps.text: Line 3: work out the brackets first. temp + 4 is 34. str() makes it the text "34".
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = int(input("Temp? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 4))
"34"

steps.text: Then + joins the text from left to right, spaces and all.
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = int(input("Temp? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 4))
It prints Pai is 34

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a problem with a clue word need a decision in the algorithm?Show the answer

What happens is not always the same. Something must be checked to choose the path.

4 minutes. From 3.1. Read each problem.

Problem A: Move 10 steps, turn 90 degrees, then say "Hello".
Problem B: If the score is bigger than 10, say "Win". Otherwise say "Try again".
Total: 3 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: which construct?

steps.text: These are different problems. Do the same steps with your problems.
steps.visual:
Problem X: Say "Ready", wait 1 second, then say "Go".
Problem Y: Play a sound only when the cat touches the ball.

steps.text: Problem X: look for a clue word. There is no clue word. Every step always happens, one after another, in order.
steps.visual: Problem X: no clue word, the steps always run in order.

steps.text: Problem Y: look for a clue word. "only when" is a clue. What happens depends on the cat touching the ball, so a decision is needed.
steps.visual: Problem Y: Play a sound only when the cat touches the ball.

steps.text: Ask the same question for each of your problems: does what happens depend on something? Then name the construct.
steps.visual: Clue words: only when ... (and the others on your notes)

steps.label: Key Facts: Sequence and Selection
steps.content:
Key Facts: Sequence and Selection

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do most algorithms use both sequence and selection?Show the answer

Most jobs have steps that always happen and also a point where something is checked.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • A construct is a way to join the steps of an algorithm.
  • Sequence: steps run in order, one after another. Change the order and the result can change.
  • Selection: a decision asks a question. The answer (True or False) chooses the path.
Clue in the problemConstruct
ifSelection
only whenSelection
otherwiseSelection (the False path)
no clue wordSequence

steps.label: Key Facts: Project Plans
steps.content:
Key Facts: Project Plans

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must some tasks wait for other tasks?Show the answer

A task can need the result of an earlier task before it can start.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • A project is a big job with a goal and an end date. A software project makes a program, an app or a game.
  • It is split into tasks: one small job each.
  • The stages: plan, design, build, test.
  • A project plan lists the tasks, their order, who does each one, the deadline and what each task needs.
  • A plan helps: you know what to do first, you finish on time, nothing is forgotten, and everyone knows who does what.

steps.label: Key Facts: Variables and Data Types
steps.content:
Key Facts: Variables and Data Types

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is a phone number stored as a String?Show the answer

Nobody does maths with a phone number, and it can start with 0.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • A variable is a named store in memory. It holds one value.
  • = means store: score = 5 puts 5 in score. A new value replaces the old one.
  • score = score + 1 uses the old value, then stores the new one.
Data typePythonStoresExample
Integerinta whole number12
Realfloata number with a decimal point2.5
Stringstrtext, in quote marks"Mia"

steps.label: Key Facts: Input and Output
steps.content:
Key Facts: Input and Output

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does "5" + "5" not give 10?Show the answer

Quote marks make text. + joins text, so the two pieces are put side by side.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • print() shows output on the screen. Text needs quote marks. A variable does not.
  • input() waits for the user to type, then gives what they typed.
  • input() always gives a String. The first thing typed goes into the first input().
FunctionIt turns a value into
int()a whole number (Integer)
float()a number with a decimal point (Real)
str()text (String), to join with + in print()

steps.label: Key Facts: Programs Using Data Types
steps.content:
Key Facts: Programs Using Data Types

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can a spelling slip in a variable name give no error at all?Show the answer

Storing to a new name just makes a new variable. Python does not know you meant the old one.

3 minutes. Add anything you had forgotten to your notes.

  • Choose the data type with two questions: Will the program do maths with it? If not, it is a String. Can it have a decimal point? Then it is a Real, if not an Integer.
  • A Real and an Integer together give a Real. / always gives a Real.
  • A number joined to text with + needs str() first.
  • Use the same name every time. score and Score are two different variables: capital letters count.
  • Using a name that was never stored stops the program with an error.
